core_obligations: Clause (3), the polytope description: introduce the polytope P defined by the hyperplane of clause (1) and the half-spaces of clause (2); show that the points M(t, omega) for all t in Tam_n are vertices of P because each is defined by n-1 independent equations, and conversely that every vertex comes from such a system (proof lines 699-701).

Clause (3), the key combinatorial input: prove that any two half-space equalities occurring at a vertex have nested or disjoint intervals, by deriving the contradiction x_{p'+1}+...+x_{p+q-1} < sum omega_k omega_l from the opposite configuration, and then identify the solution of such a system with a point M(t, omega) (proof lines 701-731).

Clause (4), the face lattice: use clause (2) to see that facets correspond bijectively to two-vertex planar trees, and that faces of codimension k correspond to planar trees with k internal edges, so that the face lattice is the lattice PT_n of planar trees (proof lines 733-736).

Clause (5), products of faces: reduce to facets, then exhibit for a facet the explicit isomorphism Theta from K_{bar omega} x K_{tilde omega} onto the facet labelled by c_{p+1+r} circ_{p+1} c_q (proof lines 738-753).
proof_roadmap: Describe the polytope P cut out by the hyperplane and the half-spaces, and prove the nested-or-disjoint alternative for the equations defining its vertices (proof lines 699-731).
Derive the face lattice from that description and finish with the explicit product decomposition of a facet (proof lines 733-753).
difficulty_reason: The proposition collects five properties of the weighted Loday realization K_omega of the associahedron: the hyperplane containing it, its description by half-spaces with equality exactly on decomposable trees, the fact that this hyperplane-and-half-space system cuts the polytope out, the identification of the face lattice with the lattice of planar trees, and the product decomposition of any face (statement lines 670-691). The proof's substance is in clauses (3) to (5): clause (3) requires showing that the equations defining a vertex have nested or disjoint intervals, which is done by deriving a strict inequality that contradicts the defining half-spaces (proof lines 699-731), clause (4) then reads the face lattice off the facet description of clause (2), and clause (5) exhibits the explicit isomorphism Theta putting a product of two smaller Loday realizations onto a facet (proof lines 738-753). Clauses (1) and (2) are dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition, and both dismissals are kept verbatim in the counted span; they are not where the item's obligation lies, since the decisive statement is the combinatorial description of the polytope, which is proved. H2.
